name: Diagnostic Equipment Manufacturing
description: Published research documents Iranian development of specialized imaging equipment, including instruments for small-animal biomedical research. Procurement records also show that installation, maintenance, regulatory acceptance, and local technical support are integral to bringing diagnostic equipment into service. [s1][s2]

seo.title: Diagnostic Equipment Manufacturing in Iran | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Explore documented Iranian imaging development, the distinction between research instruments and clinical equipment, and the evidence gaps in manufacturing statistics.

content.heading: A documented example of imaging development
content.content:
Iranian diagnostic-equipment development includes specialized instruments serving biomedical research. A paper published in 2014 evaluated HiReSPECT, a small-animal imaging system identified as a product of Parto Negar Persia in Tehran. The researchers obtained images of rat organs using radioactive tracers and assessed the instrument's ability to reveal physiological detail. Their affiliations included research centers in Bushehr and Tehran. [s1]

SPECT means single-photon emission computed tomography: detectors collect radiation emitted by a tracer, and software reconstructs its distribution. The study described both planar imaging and tomographic reconstruction. These are related imaging approaches, but a flat projection and a reconstructed volume provide different kinds of information. [s1]

The distinction between research instrumentation and clinical diagnosis matters. This was an evaluation in animals for biomedical research, not evidence of authorization for routine human scanning. It establishes a particular technical achievement; it does not establish national manufacturing capacity, current sales, or the domestic origin of every component. [s1]

content.heading: Manufacturing extends beyond delivering a machine
content.content:
A WHO invitation to bid for laboratory equipment and diagnostics for Iran in July 2020 illustrates the practical requirements surrounding equipment supply. Offers had to identify the manufacturer, country of origin, technical specifications, and warranty provisions. Brands without local agents for installation, training, and after-sales service were excluded; offered equipment also had to be acceptable to the Iranian Food and Drug Administration. [s2]

These requirements show why a manufacturing assessment should examine service capacity alongside the instrument itself. A supplier's ability to deliver a device and its ability to support use in a laboratory are separate questions. The tender is evidence of requirements for that procurement, however, rather than a complete statement of rules applying to every manufacturer or purchase in Iran. It also does not establish which bids succeeded or what equipment ultimately entered service. [s2]

content.heading: Reading procurement announcements carefully
content.content:
In November 2025, WHO published a request for information covering advanced medical imaging, radiation therapy, and treatment equipment for Iran. Its scope included delivery, installation, testing, commissioning, and maintenance. The notice explicitly described market research for planning purposes and stated that no contract would be awarded from the announcement. [s3]

This is evidence of procurement planning, not completed delivery. It cannot by itself establish either domestic manufacturing capability or dependence on imported equipment. A reliable account of the industry therefore needs product-level registration records, manufacturing-site evidence, and completed procurement or deployment documentation. Those materials remain necessary before drawing broader conclusions about the sector's scale or its geographical distribution.

name: Biotechnology
description: Within Iran's health sector, biotechnology connects biological research with medicines, diagnostics, and approaches to repairing tissue. Evidence from genomic research and vaccine development illustrates both practical applications and the need to distinguish research resources, manufacturing capabilities, and demonstrated clinical outcomes. [s1][s2][s3]

seo.title: Biotechnology in Iran: Research and Health Applications | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: An evidence-based introduction to Iran's health biotechnology, connecting genomics, biological medicines, diagnostics, and clinical evaluation.

content.heading: Several fields connected by biology
content.content:
Biotechnology uses biological systems or their components to develop products and processes. In the health branch of this guide, its scope includes biological medicines, diagnostic methods, and research into cells and tissue repair. An Iranian review published in 2012 described biopharmaceuticals, diagnosis, cell therapy, and regenerative medicine as areas of activity. That review supplies historical context, rather than a current inventory of products or institutions. [s1]

The branches overlap without being interchangeable. Genetic engineering changes biological material; genomics investigates genetic variation; molecular diagnostics applies biological measurements to diagnostic questions. A research result in one branch may support another, but a laboratory finding is not equivalent to a clinically validated product. The examples below illustrate different stages of this relationship. [s1][s2][s3]

content.heading: Genomic diversity changes the research question
content.content:
A population-genetics study published in 2019 examined variation among multiple Iranian ethnic groups using genome-wide data. Its findings demonstrated both substantial genetic overlap among several groups and differences that matter when designing association studies. The authors emphasized accounting for population structure: differences in ancestry can otherwise distort an apparent relationship between a genetic variant and a condition. [s2]

For international readers, this is a useful corrective to treating Iran as one uniform genetic population. National boundaries, language, ethnicity, and genetic ancestry describe different things. The study supports attention to diversity in research design; it does not justify assigning a fixed biological identity or a diagnosis to an individual from their ethnic label. Its participants also constitute a research sample, not a census of genetic variation throughout the country. [s2]

content.heading: From a biological platform to a manufactured product
content.content:
Vaccine technology transfer offers another window into the field. A comparative study published in 2024 examined transfer of the Cuban Soberana Plus protein-subunit vaccine to Iran, where it was named PastoCovac Plus. The authors described transfer at the formulation stage and assessed product characteristics and clinical measures before and after transfer. [s3]

This example shows why the phrase 'local production' needs a precise explanation. Formulation, manufacture of the active biological ingredient, quality testing, and clinical evaluation are distinguishable activities. Evidence for one stage should not be silently extended to every stage of a production chain. The reported comparison concerns a specified vaccine and transfer process, rather than all Iranian biological medicines. [s3]

content.heading: Institutional names require care
content.content:
The Pasteur name should not be read as proof of shared management or ongoing collaboration. In a statement dated April 2026, Institut Pasteur in Paris said that the Iranian institute had been independent since 1946 and that there was no ongoing scientific collaboration between the two institutions. The statement also expressed concern for researchers, students, and civilian employees potentially affected by strikes during the military conflict. It did not provide a facility-by-facility operational assessment. [s4]

A current account must therefore distinguish documented historical research from verified present capacity. This overview establishes selected connections between research, diversity, and production; further evidence is required for comprehensive coverage of stem-cell applications, regulation, access, and the sector's condition at the editorial cutoff.

name: Medical Biotechnology
description: Medical biotechnology applies biological systems and molecular knowledge to health-related products and investigations. Iranian examples include population-specific genomic resources and clinical evaluation of recombinant vaccines, which illustrate different routes from biological research toward medical use. [s1][s2][s3]

seo.title: Medical Biotechnology in Iran: From Research to Evidence | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Understand Iranian medical biotechnology through genomic reference resources, recombinant vaccine research, and the distinction between laboratory and clinical evidence.

content.heading: Biological tools directed toward health
content.content:
Medical biotechnology is the health-oriented application of living systems and their components. Its outputs can include diagnostic tools, biological medicines, and experimental approaches involving cells. The Iranian literature has described these as connected areas of development, but they require different kinds of evidence: a diagnostic method, a manufactured medicine, and a cell-based intervention cannot be assessed by the same endpoint. [s1]

A useful way to explore the subject is to ask what a project produces and what has actually been demonstrated. A database may improve interpretation of genetic findings without itself being a treatment. A vaccine candidate may reach human trials without establishing lasting protection against every later viral variant. These distinctions help separate scientific capability from claims about routine medical benefit. [s2][s3]

content.heading: A reference resource is part of medical infrastructure
content.content:
Iranome provides a concrete example of work supporting genomic medicine. Its investigators at the University of Social Welfare and Rehabilitation Sciences in Tehran and the University of Toronto developed a database using whole-exome sequencing, which examines protein-coding regions of DNA. The project's stated motivation was the underrepresentation of Iranian populations in existing genomic reference resources. [s2]

Such resources help researchers interpret genetic variation in context. A variant that appears rare in a poorly representative database may be more frequent in an underrepresented population. Iranome's institutional account explains its intended contribution to this problem; that intention should be distinguished from measured improvements in diagnosis or health outcomes. [s2]

The website inspected after the editorial cutoff describes successive project phases without dating the update. It is therefore used here to explain the project's purpose and approach, not to establish its exact size or release state on the cutoff date. [s2]

content.heading: Recombinant vaccines and the clinical evidence boundary
content.content:
A phase III study published in 2024 evaluated Razi Cov Pars, a recombinant spike-protein COVID-19 vaccine manufactured by the Razi Vaccine and Serum Research Institute in Karaj. Recombinant production uses genetic instructions to produce a selected protein; this differs from using an inactivated whole virus. The study compared the vaccine with Sinopharm's BBIBP vaccine in Iranian adults. [s3]

The investigators used a non-inferiority design, which asks whether a product performs no worse than a comparator beyond a prespecified margin. The publication also included a separate non-randomized component. Those components should not be treated as equally protected against differences between participant groups. The reported primary endpoint concerned symptomatic, PCR-confirmed COVID-19 during the trial's defined observation period. [s3]

The study documents clinical development, but it should not be converted into a claim about present-day effectiveness, current availability, or comparative performance against later variants. This page does not extract efficacy figures because the complete results and limitations were not consistently retrievable during inspection. A fuller account requires examination of those materials and independent assessment before drawing clinical conclusions. [s3]
